title: Newly Reconstituted National Commission for Minorities Holds First Meeting of 2026, Reviews Welfare and Safeguards for Minority Communities
body_text:
The first meeting of the newly re-constituted Commission held today under the chairmanship of Shri Harjit Singh Grewal, Chairman, NCM.
The meeting was attended by Ms. S. Munawari Begum, Vice Chairperson; Shri Berjis Desai, Member, and Shri Glenn E Souza Ticlo, Member. Shri Suchindra Misra, Secretary NCM and Dr. Atya Nand, Joint Secretary NCM were also present in the meeting along with other officers of the Commission.
During the meeting, the Commission reviewed matters pertaining to the welfare and interests of the minority communities and deliberated upon issues placed before it for consideration. The Members exchanged views on the ongoing activities of the Commission and discussed the way forward on pending matters.
The Chairperson emphasized the Commission’s mandate to work for the development of minorities and to monitor the working of safeguards for protection of their interests.
*****
AK/MR

enrichment.summary: The reconstituted National Commission for Minorities (NCM), chaired by Shri Harjit Singh Grewal, held its first meeting of 2026, attended by the Vice Chairperson and Members along with the Secretary and Joint Secretary. The Commission reviewed welfare matters concerning minority communities and discussed pending issues and the way forward. The Chairperson reiterated NCM's mandate to promote minority development and monitor safeguards protecting their interests.
enrichment.context:
The National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body constituted under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, tasked with evaluating the progress of minority development, monitoring the working of safeguards provided in the Constitution and laws, and looking into specific complaints of deprivation of rights. Six communities—Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Zoroastrians (Parsis), and Jains—are notified as minorities under the Act. The Commission periodically undergoes reconstitution as members' terms expire, and its first meeting after reconstitution typically involves reviewing ongoing cases and setting priorities rather than announcing new policy.

This release is purely a procedural update reporting the first meeting of newly appointed members, without disclosing any new policy decisions, schemes, or substantive findings. Such administrative announcements have low direct examinable value but may be useful for aspirants to recall the composition and mandate of the NCM as a statutory body relevant to governance and social justice topics.
